strengths: The paper is written in a plain, easy to read style. The organization of the material is rational, the mathematical section contains good explanations and and the line of reasoning is apparently easy to follow.
The integration of the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem with neural networks, and more specifically in autoencoder architectures is interesting and underexplored.
The report on employing Learnable Activations to high-dimensional data processing is favoured.
The paper is generally written and easy to understand.
The proposed method for generating learnable activation functions makes sense.
The experiments are valid, although limited to image dimensionality reduction tasks.
All technical sections are easy to follow, the mathematical notation is clear. I appreciate the rather “verbose” notation in section 3.3 - the strategy is clear at first sight.
weaknesses: The primary weakness of this paper is its narrow scope. The arguments for the efficacy of the proposed method are only centered on its ability to produce better reproduction accuracies compared to other models, while potentially interesting insights on the characteristics of the produced activation functions are entirely missing.

Specifically, the paper lacks a thorough investigation into the learned activation functions. The authors only demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy, but do not analyze the properties of the learned activation functions themselves. For example, it is unclear if the learned functions are significantly different from each other, or if they converge to similar shapes. Furthermore, the paper does not explore the potential for these learned activation functions to generalize to other tasks beyond dimensionality reduction, which limits the broader impact of the work. The absence of such analysis makes it difficult to understand the true contribution of the proposed method beyond achieving slightly better reconstruction scores.

Empirical studies on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST do not match the title "Enhancing High-dimensional Data Processing" title and significantly lack sufficient empirical studies to support the superiority of KARA. Experiments covering CIFAR-100 and ImageNet and comparisons to SOTAs are expected.

The novelty and contributions to the field are questionable when the content is limited to the employment of Kolmogorov-Arnold theorem on auto-encoder architectures and discussion on shift-invariance and sparsification. Either theoretical analysis towards KARA's properties or sufficient experiments are essential.
No detailed experiment setup is provided in the paper (appendix).

Section 3.1, 3.2 and 3.4 describe advancements presented in the original KAN paper, Section 3.3 describes convolutional KANs (https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13155) (without reference to the corresponding paper). Combining two KANs into an Autoencoder to analyse the latent space is a viable application of KANs and yields interesting results. However, to justify a publication in a conference like ICLR, I would expect either a contribution to the model, or a more detailed analysis of the outcome.

The related work section does not reference any prior research on KANs, such as U-KAN (https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02918), KAT (https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.10594), or KAN Autoencoders (https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.02077) (see also https://github.com/mintisan/awesome-kan).
